candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB) – hivatalos portál
candidates.why_relevant: Home of Hungary's public procurement remedies tribunal (KDB), the primary first-instance body deciding appeals against banking/payment-services tenders (account management, card acceptance, POS, cash logistics). Acts as the master pointer to decisions, pending applications, ex-officio initiations and the related court judgments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl of section index pages; snowball into decision PDFs and attached court judgments; respect robots.txt and low request rate
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language web search on cell seed query, then snowball
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság határozatok kereső bankszámla-vezetés jogorvoslat

candidates.source_name: Döntőbizottsági határozatok (KDB decisions listing)
candidates.why_relevant: Full text KDB decisions (D.xxx/yyyy numbering) naming contracting authority, bidders, contested evaluation criteria, prices and the outcome (annulment, fine, rejection). For banking/payments this is the richest disclosure layer behind an award notice.
candidates.access_status: public listing; individual decisions as PDF/HTML
candidates.legal_status: official public record, pseudonymisation applied in parts
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Incremental scrape by decision number/date; store PDF + extract parties, CPV, contract value; keyword filter on banking/payments vocabulary
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language web search + snowball from KDB portal
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság határozatok kereső bankszámla-vezetés jogorvoslat

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Hatóság – Döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok adatbázis (structured search)
candidates.why_relevant: The structured, filterable database of KDB AND court decisions. Verified by fetch that it exposes ~20+ filters: case number (ügyiratszám), contracting authority and applicant names, procedure type, decision type and date ranges, subject matter, legal basis, court decision number, EU preliminary-ruling flag, CPV codes and tags. CPV filtering (66xxxxxx financial/insurance services) makes banking/payments extraction tractable.
candidates.access_status: public web form; no documented API or bulk export observed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Form-driven harvesting: iterate CPV 66xxxxxx + date windows, capture result rows and linked decision documents; save-search feature suggests stable query params worth reverse-engineering
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search then direct WebFetch of the search page to inventory filters
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság határozatok kereső bankszámla-vezetés jogorvoslat

candidates.source_name: KDB – Jogorvoslati kérelmek (pending remedy applications)
candidates.why_relevant: Early-warning layer: applications filed but not yet decided. Signals a contested banking/payments tender weeks-to-months before the decision and before any contract-award correction notice appears.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily/weekly diff of the listing page; alert on banking/payment keywords in case subject
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság határozatok kereső bankszámla-vezetés jogorvoslat

candidates.source_name: Fővárosi Törvényszék judgments published as KDB case attachments
candidates.why_relevant: The Fővárosi Törvényszék has exclusive jurisdiction over judicial review of KDB decisions; its judgments are mirrored as attachments on the KDB site under a predictable attachment path with case numbers such as 103.K.704.694/2024/10 linked to D.634/2024. Judgments often restate bid prices and evaluation detail and show whether an award was ultimately annulled.
candidates.access_status: public PDF attachments; opaque hashed paths so must be discovered via case pages
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Harvest attachment links from each KDB case page rather than guessing URLs; OCR-safe PDF text extraction
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on court/procurement terms, snowballed to the attachment path pattern
queries_used: Kúria Bírósági Határozatok Gyűjteménye közbeszerzés Fővárosi Törvényszék közigazgatási per ítélet kereső

candidates.source_name: Bírósági Határozatok Gyűjteménye (BHGY) – national court decisions collection
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory collection of anonymised judgments including administrative-litigation judgments on single-instance administrative decisions — the category that covers KDB judicial review. Full-text indexed with statute-based and free-text search, so 'Kbt.' + banking terms can be searched directly.
candidates.access_status: public; exact landing path uncertain (birosag.hu/ugyfeleknek/birosagi-hatarozatok-gyujtemenye is the descriptive page)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Free-text query harvesting on Kbt./közbeszerzés + pénzforgalmi/bankszámla/kártyaelfogadás terms; a published user guide PDF documents the search syntax
queries_used: Kúria Bírósági Határozatok Gyűjteménye közbeszerzés Fővárosi Törvényszék közigazgatási per ítélet kereső

candidates.source_name: Kúria – anonimizált határozatok / precedent decisions
candidates.why_relevant: Supreme court (Kúria) review (felülvizsgálat, Kfv. numbering) sets the doctrine that shapes how banking/payment procurement disputes are decided, and its own case pages include preliminary-reference cases such as Kfv.III.37.415/2017 arising from the interchange-fee litigation.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword + Kfv. case-number crawl; also monitor jogegységi/collegiate opinions on Kbt.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on competition + court terms
queries_used: GVH versenyfelügyeleti eljárás határozat kártyaelfogadás bankközi jutalék bank döntés adatbázis

candidates.access_status: public, includes an archive section for older years
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl decision index by year and Vj- case number; filter on banking/payment keywords; track subsequent court annulments
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language seed query on GVH card acceptance
queries_used: GVH versenyfelügyeleti eljárás határozat kártyaelfogadás bankközi jutalék bank döntés adatbázis

negative_findings.description: The Közbeszerzési Hatóság 'Döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok' search page was fetched and its ~20 filter fields inventoried, but the page documents no API, no bulk export and no stated download format for decisions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Rich filtering (including CPV) but retrieval appears to be one-record-at-a-time through a web form; a save-search feature exists which hints at parameterised URLs worth reverse-engineering.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for the highest-value source in this cell will need form-driven harvesting rather than a feed, raising cost and fragility.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian-language searches combining KDB remedies terms with banking terms (bankszámla-vezetés, jogorvoslat) returned only the institutional/portal layer, not individual banking-sector decisions.

negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the cell cannot be covered by search-engine monitoring alone — the KDB/KH databases must be queried directly with CPV 66xxxxxx and banking keywords.

negative_findings.description: No public repository of individual EUTAF audit reports or irregularity (szabálytalansági) decisions was found; only summary presentations, internal instructions and an ÁSZ audit of EUTAF itself.
negative_findings.result_summary: EUTAF publishes institutional material, not case-level audit findings.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Audit-level detail on EU-funded procurement (including any banking/IT payments contracts) is largely non-public and would need FOI requests.

brief: Hungary's procurement-remedies and audit layer is unusually well institutionalised and almost entirely Hungarian-language. The core is the Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság (KDB), whose full-text decisions and pending remedy applications are published on dontobizottsag.kozbeszerzes.hu and mirrored into the Közbeszerzési Hatóság's structured 'Döntőbizottsági és bírósági határozatok' database, which offers roughly twenty filters including contracting authority, bidder, subject matter and CPV code — the practical entry point for isolating banking and payment-service tenders. Judicial review sits exclusively with the Fővárosi Törvényszék (judgments republished as PDF attachments on KDB case pages) and onward at the Kúria and in the Bírósági Határozatok Gyűjteménye, while the audit and competition flanks are covered by ÁSZ reports, the Integritás Hatóság's system-wide annual integrity analysis, EUTAF for EU-funded programmes, and the GVH decision database, which holds the landmark Vj-018/2008 interchange-fee cartel case against 22 banks plus Visa and Mastercard and the 2019 card-acceptance sector inquiry. The main constraint is access rather than availability: no API, feed or bulk export was found for any of the primary decision repositories, and individual banking-sector decisions are not surfaced by general web search, so this cell must be collected by direct, form-driven querying of the KDB and GVH databases supplemented by NGO aggregators (Tenderbajnok, K-Monitor, Átlátszó) as lead generators.
